notes: visual-qa 2026-08-01 flags one HIGH issue (twice, at 375 + 393px): the floating 'Assistent' button overlapping a mid-agenda row's bottom-right corner (today the 14:15 'Tour de France Femmes 2026' row's 'neste: … · TV 2 Play' subtext tail). At 900px the labelled pill sits cleanly in the empty right margin (QA: low/no issue).

No PR opened. Verified current state with viewport (non-full-page) screenshots at 375/393/900: the phone-width mitigation is already in place — the button is glyph-only, 44px (HIG min), tucked into the extreme corner with a soft (not heavy) shadow; at 900 the pill lives in the empty margin beside the 640px-capped column; the LAST agenda row and footer are never occluded (main.wrap padding-bottom:88px). Header/tabs/DIREKTE NÅ/day-groups all intact and calm.

This is the same inherent, DESIGN-sanctioned overlap the prior ui-fix run already minimised (PR #432, 2026-07-31, which shrank the phone FAB). A fixed bottom-trailing button over an edge-to-edge single column unavoidably sits over SOME row on load — DESIGN.md §345–370 (WP-146 variant D, owner decision) explicitly sanctions this: the button floats over content and 'Agendaen … scroller rolig UNDER knappen'; only the LAST row is guaranteed clear, and that guarantee holds.

Both of visual-qa's proposed remedies are exhausted: bottom-padding is already applied (88px) and cannot fix a position:fixed element's overlap with a MID-list row; shrink-below-a-breakpoint is already done (glyph-only 44px). The only remaining ways to remove the overlap — dock the control into the flow, use a full-width bottom bar, reserve a permanent right gutter on phones, or hide the FAB — are all explicitly forbidden by DESIGN.md and/or drop the assistant entry on phones (a functional + web-parity regression). Each is an owner-level design decision, outside the ui-fix loop's remit (CLAUDE.md: DESIGN.md is normative, never deviate without explicit owner instruction).

Conservative no-op by design: shipping another cosmetic tweak would be churn that cannot resolve the inherent overlap and risks a live-site regression on an auto-merging PR. A missing fix beats a regression. Escalation for the owner: if this HIGH finding should stop recurring, it needs a DESIGN.md decision on the phone-width assistant entry pattern (e.g. reserve a right gutter on phones, or accept the sanctioned float-over and downgrade the QA severity to reflect DESIGN.md §370).
